source: psz-re — enemy/boss_dragon.narc via ArchiveUnpacker zpr()+narc(), skeleton via apicula
naming_note: Reyburn's bones are romanized Japanese (L_ude, atama, sippo) while Octo Diablo's are English (Left_arm, top_head). Different asset authors, same L/R pairing convention.

entity_map_B5.request: godot-parity-requests.md B5 - psz-godot assumes the Octo-derived entity offsets hold for boss_dragon, and asks for confirmation
entity_map_B5.answer: PARTLY, AND THE PART psz-godot MOST NEEDS IS REFUTED. The common header transfers; the tail does not.
entity_map_B5.confidence: confirmed for the header, refuted for the tail
entity_map_B5.oracle: five savestates of one Reyburn fight at HP 1650 / 1576 / 1439 / 1429 / 1419, entity located by scanning main RAM for vtable 0x0219F8D4. The body is at 0x0237a9d0, whose +0x34 is 0x0237aa04 - the address this file already cites for HP, so the entity is identified by an independently recorded landmark rather than by picking the plausible hit.
entity_map_B5.a_scanning_trap_worth_recording: 0x02198018, 0x02198050 and 0x02198088 also contain the vtable word and are NOT entities. Their +0x18 / +0x34 read 63707 / 48400 and similar, and their positions are in the hundreds of thousands. Filter vtable hits by 0 < current <= max <= 20000 or three ghosts survive.

REFUTED_on_reyburn.the_claim: +0xD4 mode, +0xD8 state, +0xE0 selected action, +0xE4 phase row - carried over from Octo Diablo
REFUTED_on_reyburn.why_this_is_conclusive: all five are valid main-RAM addresses, they form an ascending series, they are byte-identical across a 231-point HP drop spanning four separate captures, and they dereference to structured blocks rather than to noise. A phase row index and a mode flag do not behave like that.
REFUTED_on_reyburn.the_consequence_for_psz_godot: reading phase from +0xE4 on Reyburn yields 0x0237bd00. That is not a wrong number, it is a pointer - so any attack-table lookup indexed by it is unbounded, and any 'phase == 1' test is permanently true.
REFUTED_on_reyburn.what_they_probably_are: LEAD, not established: five sub-object pointers. Reyburn has 21 bones against Octo's 14 and is the only boss with a separate part-joint record, so a parts array in the class tail is the obvious reading. Nothing here ties a pointer to a named part.

CANDIDATES_for_the_real_state_fields.method: diffed the first 0x140 bytes of the entity across all five states; only six words differ, four of which are the confirmed HP / position / facing
CANDIDATES_for_the_real_state_fields.+0xD0 u16: 583, 474, 578, 584, 575 - varies but not monotonically with HP. Timer- or frame-counter-shaped.
CANDIDATES_for_the_real_state_fields.+0xEC low byte: 8, 8, 8, 10, 10 - changes once, late in the sequence. The most enum-shaped field in the record and the best candidate for state or selected action.
CANDIDATES_for_the_real_state_fields.confidence: guess. Identified by variance across five states, nothing more. Neither has been watched changing against a known event.

NOT_MEASURED_and_psz_godot_should_keep_g.phase threshold: unmeasured. psz-godot's 35 percent enrage is unsupported, but so is copying Octo's max/2 - the tail layout already differs between the two classes, so nothing licenses assuming the phase RULE transfers when the phase FIELD does not.
NOT_MEASURED_and_psz_godot_should_keep_g.does he fly: +0x3C (Y) is 0 in all five states, so Reyburn is on the ground at every HP from 100 percent down to 86 percent. That is a genuine constraint on the 'timed flight cycle' psz-godot invented, but it is not evidence about what happens below 86 percent.
NOT_MEASURED_and_psz_godot_should_keep_g.what_would_close_it: one fight driven past half HP with +0xD0 and +0xEC sampled alongside +0x34 and +0x3C. The static route is exhausted - every savestate on disk is above 86 percent.

attack_selection_B1.request: godot-parity-requests.md B1 — 'breakpoint the selection slot in Reyburn's vtable (0x0219F8D4, ov20), read the table it indexes by +0xE4'
attack_selection_B1.answer: REFUTED AS POSED. Reyburn is not table-driven. Slot 11 is not a selector on this class, there is no Octo-shaped weight table in its overlay, and nothing in ov20 reads the roll source at all.
attack_selection_B1.confidence: confirmed for the negatives; the +0xEC positive is confirmed as a bitfield, unnamed per bit
attack_selection_B1.method_was_validated_on_OCTO_FIRST: every step was run against Octo Diablo, where the answer is already recorded, before being run against Reyburn. A scan for u32 rows summing to 100 finds Octo's table at exactly 0x0219FFF4 with rows [90,0,10] and [0,90,10] and only 3 hits in 39 KB. Vtable index 11 of 0x021A1280 resolves to 0x021983f5, the recorded selection function. Decompiling it reproduces the recorded shape: a 3-iteration loop over PTR_DAT_ov21__0219fff4 indexed iVar5*4 + *(entity+0xe4)*0xc, running total compared against *(*(entity+0x10)+0x88), gated on *(entity+0xd8) == 0.
attack_selection_B1.NEGATIVE_1_no_weight_table_in_ov20: scanned ov20 (32,704 bytes, 0x02197f80..0x0219ff40) for rows summing to 100 at widths 2..5 as u32 and u16: ZERO hits. Also zero for u32 rows summing to 1000 or 10000. Byte-width scans return 27-43 hits but every one is at an unaligned address inside an instruction stream, which is what noise looks like. The same scan finds Octo's table immediately.
attack_selection_B1.NEGATIVE_2_nothing_in_ov20_reads_the_rol: decompiled all 213 ov20 functions and searched for the roll source *(*(entity+0x10)+0x88) that Octo's selector compares its running total against. ZERO functions reference it. So it is not that the table moved — the weighted-roll mechanism is absent from this class.

SLOT_11_IS_A_FLAG_SETTER_NOT_A_SELECTOR.what_it_does: keyed on param_2 — 0 calls FUN_02035880/FUN_020358e8/FUN_02036b24 and sets +0xEC |= 0x40; 2 sets |= 0x01; 4 sets |= 0x02
SLOT_11_IS_A_FLAG_SETTER_NOT_A_SELECTOR.so: the slot that selects an attack on Octo enters a state and raises a flag on Reyburn

POSITIVE_+0xEC_IS_REYBURNS_BEHAVIOUR_STA.reach: 24 of the 213 ov20 functions read or write it — by far the most-touched field in the class

bits_observed.0x001: set by slot 11 (param_2==2); cleared in 0219ae94; tested in 0219aec4
bits_observed.0x002: set by slot 11 (param_2==4); cleared in 0219ced4; tested in 0219cf80 and 0219e27c
bits_observed.0x004: set and cleared in 02199030; tested in 02198a38
bits_observed.0x008: set and cleared in 021980c8; tested in 0219ab24
bits_observed.0x010: set in 0219a874 / 0219aec4 / 0219c3dc; cleared in 0219ab24 / 0219b574 / 0219cdbc; tested in 021987d0 / 0219aa48
bits_observed.0x040: set by slot 11 (param_2==0); tested in 02198300, 02199c98, 0219a2bc, 0219a3ec — the most-tested bit

POSITIVE_+0xEC_IS_REYBURNS_BEHAVIOUR_STA.no_bit_is_NAMED: which behaviour each bit gates is not established. This is the field's shape and its call sites, not its semantics.

attack_selection_B1.IT_CONFIRMS_THE_B5_CANDIDATE_FROM_A_SECO: entity_map_B5 flagged +0xEC as a candidate purely from variance — its low byte read 8, 8, 8, 10, 10 across five savestates, with no idea what it was. The code says +0xEC is an OR-accumulated flag word, and 8 -> 10 is exactly bit 1 (0x02) being set, which slot 11 does on param_2 == 4. A static variance scan and a static code read, run for different reasons, land on the same field and agree on the mechanism.
attack_selection_B1.WHAT_psz_godot_SHOULD_DO: stop looking for a Reyburn weight table; there is not one to port. Its attack behaviour is a flag machine on +0xEC driven by whatever calls the vtable with param_2. Hand-weighting attacks is a reasonable stand-in ONLY as an admitted invention — it cannot be replaced by a measured table, because the original does not select that way.

animation_slot_table_DECODED.closes: boss-porting.md's open 'enemy_data_*.rel (DSIF)' for the dragon, and supplies the index space parity request B4 needs
animation_slot_table_DECODED.what_it_is: an ANIMATION table — each entry is a member index into enemy/boss_dragon.narc, in RUNTIME order
animation_slot_table_DECODED.PROOF_IS_AN_EXACT_CONTENT_MATCH: the 26 values are injective and span 43..69. boss_dragon.narc holds exactly 26 z_*.nsbca members and sorted(values) EQUALS that list exactly. Same identity argument that decoded the octopus table, run independently here.
animation_slot_table_DECODED.AND_THE_FILE_DECLARES_IT: region-A offset 196 is a 56-byte block of seven {offset, count} pairs: (76,2) (84,1) (88,26) (0,0) (0,0) (0,0) (192,1). The third pair names the animation table's offset AND its count of 26. So the count is confirmed twice over — once by the narc identity and once by the file's own directory.
animation_slot_table_DECODED.the_order_is_FUNCTIONAL_not_alphabetical: boss_reyburn.json's existing 'animations' list is the 26 names sorted alphabetically, which carries no structure. The table's order does: locomotion (0-2), flight (3-4), reactions (5-7), breath (8-10), attacks (11-15), then transitions and the rest (16-25). That grouping is evidence the runtime indexes this table by a slot number rather than by name.
animation_slot_table_DECODED.FLIGHT_HAS_DEDICATED_SLOTS: z_001_flst and z_001_fly occupy slots 3 and 4. So flight is an addressable state in the shipped data, which is more than entity_map_B5 could say — that could only report Reyburn grounded at every HP above 86 percent. It still does not show he ENTERS the state in play.
animation_slot_table_DECODED.what_this_does_NOT_give: per-attack damage, reach, arc or active frames. Parity request B3's static half is only partly answered: the animation table is decoded, the attack parameters are not located.

MAX_HP_IS_IN_NEITHER_REL.finding: 1650 does not appear in enemy_data_boss_dragon.rel as a u16 or a u32, at any alignment. Nor does 5220 in enemy_data_boss_octopus.rel.
MAX_HP_IS_IN_NEITHER_REL.why_it_matters: boss-porting.md recorded 'Max HP 5220 is NOT in it as a plain u16, so the pool is derived or scaled' from the octopus alone. A second boss behaves the same way, so it is a property of the format rather than a quirk of one file.

part_hitbox_table_DECODED.*** CORRECTED — THE EARLIER READING WAS: the previous version of this entry claimed 13 entries indexed by a part index 0..12. Both halves are wrong. The array holds SIXTEEN records, and byte 1 is a GROUP ID that repeats, not each record's own index.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.how_the_error_happened: the finder required byte1 == k, i.e. that the index counts 0,1,2,... It therefore stopped at the first repeat — dragon's byte1 runs 0..12 then 12, 12, 13 — and silently returned the first 13 records as if that were the whole array. A signature that assumes injectivity does not merely miss the non-injective case, it TRUNCATES it, and a truncated array looks exactly like a complete one.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.and_it_is_the_same_disease_the_locator_h: commit a797389 found the shared part-table locator was landing on the wrong array in 61 of 67 archives, and diagnosed it as 'a locator checked on the one case it works for' — boss_octopus, whose ids happen to be injective. My finder was a different implementation that made the SAME assumption and was validated against the SAME archive. Reproducing octopus exactly is what convinced me it was right; octopus is precisely the case that cannot distinguish the two readings.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.location: enemy_data_boss_dragon.rel, region-A offset 476, 16 records x 8 bytes
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.record: byte0 = payload flag, byte1 = GROUP ID (repeats), +4 = relocated pointer to 1.19.12 dimensions
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.payload_rule_still_holds: flag 0 -> one value, flag 1 -> three. Checked over all SIXTEEN records this time: consecutive payload-pointer gaps are 4 bytes after every flag-0 record and 12 after the one flag-1 record, no exception. That rule was right; it was verified over a truncated set and survives the correction.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.what_changed_numerically: three records were missing entirely — the second and third of group 12 (3.25 and 1.75) and all of group 13 (2.25). And 'part 12 = 4.25' was wrong as stated: group 12 has THREE members and 4.25 is only the first. 14 distinct groups, 16 records.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.what_this_costs_psz_godot: the previous entry told psz-godot these were 'real measured hitbox radii' that 'can replace guessed numbers directly'. For groups 0..11 and their single values that still holds. For group 12 it did not, and a port keying on a part index rather than a group id would have silently dropped three of the sixteen.
part_hitbox_table_DECODED.still_not_established: what a group IS. Three records under one id is the shape of a limb segment or a multi-part hitbox, but nothing here ties a group to a bone or to an attack, and 13 records against 21 bones already ruled out a one-to-one bone mapping. The attack-to-group mapping remains unmeasured, so B3 is still only partly answered.

HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST_but_not_as_a.why_this_entry_exists: a narrow search for '+0x18 / 2' returns nothing in ov20, which would support 'Reyburn has no HP check at all'. Widening to ANY read of +0x18 refutes that before it was written down.
HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST_but_not_as_a.the_finding: FUN_ov20__0219a3ec reads the entity's max HP as a signed short and multiplies it by a 1.19.12 constant using the 64-bit helper FUN_0200a380, rounding with (x + 0x800) >> 12:  if (*(int *)(param_1 + 0x9c) < maxHP * 0.2) { ... }

the_constants_are_exact.0x0219A750: 410 = 0.100098 in 1.19.12, i.e. 0.1 — applied to a value fetched through the part-table root at entity+0x14, not to HP
the_constants_are_exact.0x0219A758: 819 = 0.199951, i.e. 0.2 — this is the one applied to MAX HP
the_constants_are_exact.0x0219A760: 1365 = 0.333252, i.e. 1/3 — used as a plain field value nearby

HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST_but_not_as_a.*** WHAT IT IS NOT ***: it is NOT a phase threshold and NOT 'current HP below 20 percent'. The comparison is against the CONTROLLER's field at +0x9C, not the entity's current HP at +0x34 — and param_1 is the controller here, the entity being *(param_1 + 4), the same indirection recorded for the Octo hooks. What +0x9C holds is unidentified, so all that is established is that a 20-percent-of-max-HP quantity is computed and compared against something.
HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST_but_not_as_a.what_it_does_and_does_not_change: psz-godot's 35 percent enrage is still unsupported and Octo's max/2 still does not transfer — both stand. What changes is that 'Reyburn ignores HP entirely' is NOT available as a conclusion: the class does compute a fraction of max HP, and identifying +0x9C is now the concrete next step for B2 rather than a blind hunt.
HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST_but_not_as_a.the_process_point: the narrow pattern was chosen because it matched the Octo code exactly, which is precisely why it was the wrong test for a different class. A negative is only worth its coverage, and this one had to be widened twice before it was safe to state.

THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.answers: the open question left by HP_FRACTION_CONSTANTS_EXIST — what writes the controller's +0x9C
THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.the_hook: FUN_ov20__0219a114 (286 bytes), Reyburn's damage hook — the structural twin of Octo's FUN_ov21__0219a340: same (int, short*, int*, undefined4) signature and the same iVar4 = *(int *)(param_1 + 4) entity indirection.
THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.*** THE SIGN IS SETTLED FROM INSIDE THE: +0x94 is guarded by 0 < +0x94, INCREMENTED by *param_2, and fires a callback the moment it falls below 1. A pool that starts positive and has to DECREASE to trip that test can only do so if *param_2 is NEGATIVE. So damage arrives as a negative short, and the fields written with -= — +0x9C, +0xA0, +0xA4 — COUNT UP as damage lands. This matters: read naively, '+0x9c -= damage' looks like a pool draining, and every conclusion from it would invert.
THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.SO_+0x9C_IS_CUMULATIVE_DAMAGE_TAKEN: which makes FUN_ov20__0219a3ec's gate — if (+0x9c < maxHP * 0.2) — read as 'while Reyburn has taken less than 20 percent of his max HP in total damage'. With max HP 1650 that is 330 damage. It is a real measured behavioural threshold, expressed in damage dealt rather than in HP remaining, which is why searching for an HP-remaining comparison never found it.
THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.it_is_NOT_the_phase_gate: the 20-percent test is one of three conjuncts on that branch — it also needs +0xAC < 10 and (entity+0xEC & 0x80) == 0 — and the branch body loops over four slots through FUN_020352a4 and FUN_020865fc, which looks like spawning or target selection rather than a phase change. So this gates ONE behaviour, and calling it 'enrage' would be the same overreach as calling +0xE4 a phase row on this class.
THE_DAMAGE_HOOK_AND_WHAT_+0x9C_IS.a_second_mechanic_falls_out: +0x94 is a separate pool that only moves on hit type 1 (param_3[9] == 1), and when it is exhausted it calls FUN_ov20__021986bc(entity) — a one-shot on depletion. That is the shape of a breakable part or a stagger meter, and it is unexplored.

the_four_counters.+0x94: hit-type-1 pool, positive-guarded, one-shot callback on depletion
the_four_counters.+0x9C: cumulative damage — the one the 20% gate reads
the_four_counters.+0xA0: cumulative damage as well (same update, no guard)
the_four_counters.+0xA4: cumulative damage restricted to hit type 1

B2_AS_FAR_AS_THE_CAPTURES_GO.the_bound_first: the seven Reyburn captures span HP 1650 down to 1419 of 1650 -- 100% to 86.0%. B2 asks where the phase changes trigger and notes psz-godot assumes 35%; Octo flips at exactly max/2. NEITHER IS IN THE SAMPLE. No savestate on disk has him below 86%, so no threshold can be measured from what exists, and recording that stops the next person measuring one from data that never reaches it.
B2_AS_FAR_AS_THE_CAPTURES_GO.what_the_captures_do_give: across that 231-point drop only SIX of the 72 words in the entity's first 0x120 bytes change at all: +0x34 (HP), +0x38, +0x40 and +0x44 (position and facing), +0xD0 and +0xEC. Everything else in the entity head is byte-identical over the whole span, which is what makes those six the candidate list.

the_two_non_obvious_ones.+0xD0: 583, 474, 578, 584, 575 -- oscillating in a narrow band and NOT monotone with HP. Consistent with boss-porting's 'u16, timer-shaped'.
the_two_non_obvious_ones.+0xEC: 0x308, 0x308, 0x308, 0x30A, 0x30A -- monotone, and the ONLY non-position field besides HP that moves and never goes back. boss-porting recorded 'low byte, 8 -> 10'; this reproduces it exactly with the surrounding halfword. It is the strongest phase-or-counter candidate, and at 86% HP what it counts is unread.

B2_AS_FAR_AS_THE_CAPTURES_GO.the_pointer_block_reconfirmed: +0xD4, +0xD8, +0xDC, +0xE0 and +0xE4 hold 0x0237B9A0, 0x0237BA30, 0x0237BBF0, 0x0237BCB0 and 0x0237BD00, byte-identical across all seven captures and all valid main-RAM pointers. Octo Diablo's phase/mode/state map does not transfer to Reyburn, as boss-porting already recorded -- now reproduced with values across a wider set.
B2_AS_FAR_AS_THE_CAPTURES_GO.so_B2_needs_a_fight: the static half of B2 is exhausted by this. Answering it needs HP driven below 86%, which is the dynamic measurement the request asks for.

B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.what: the first dynamic B2 measurement. HP was written down the whole health range on a live Reyburn and the entity head watched for a phase flip.
B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.how: gdb-headless.sh --state (major-13 ss13 build, isolated port 3477/display :131), entity located at 0x0237A9D0 by the vtable, HP written at entity+0x34, emulator continued ~1.5s between samples so the game could react.

sweep_2_whole_head.result: against the 90% baseline, EXACTLY ONE word differs at every one of 55/45/40/30 — and it is inside {+0x34 HP, +0x38..+0x44 position/facing}. Nothing else in the head moves.

B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.*** THE RESULT IS NEGATIVE, AND THAT IS: no HP threshold was found ANYWHERE tested — not in the entity's first 0x140 bytes, and not in the five blocks its +0xD4..+0xE4 pointers reach. Octo Diablo's rule (cross max/2 and three fields flip) does not reproduce, and psz-godot's assumed 35% is not corroborated by anything. The one candidate that appeared was refuted by bisection, above.
B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.*** THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS ***: writing HP is very likely the WRONG INSTRUMENT for B2, and Octo shows why: its threshold lives in FUN_ov21__02199f84, a hook on the DAMAGE path. Poking HP behind the game's back never calls that hook, so a boss built the same way could not flip no matter how the HP is driven. This refutes 'Reyburn's phase is a function of current HP that can be triggered by setting HP' — it does NOT establish that Reyburn has no phases.
B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.REFUTED — +0xEC is not monotone: recorded from the captures as 'low byte, 8 -> 10, MONOTONE' over 100%..86%. Live across the full range it takes 0x30a, 0x30b, 0x317 and 0x31f, moving DOWN as well as up. The monotonicity was an artefact of a 231-point sample at the very top of his health.
B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.STRENGTHENED — the pointer block: +0xD4..+0xE4 was recorded as invariant across the captures, which only span 100%..86%. It is now invariant live from 90% down to 8%, so 'Octo's phase/mode/state map does not transfer to Reyburn' holds over the whole health range and not just the top of it.
B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.what_would_settle_it: stop writing HP. Either deal real damage across the crossing, or set a Z0 breakpoint on the damage-apply path (slot 4 / FUN_020437d8) and watch 0237b9a0 across it — Z0 is the breakpoint melonDS actually honours, and the Octo precedent says the write will land on a controller, not on the entity.

step_2_the_pointed_to_blocks.why: Octo's transition is NOT written to the entity. FUN_ov21__02199f84 latches mode on *param_1*, a controller reached as *(param_1+4)==entity — boss-porting flags that exact base trap. Reyburn's +0xD4..+0xE4 hold five POINTERS, so a controller is where a phase would live.
step_2_the_pointed_to_blocks.read: 0x80 at each of 0237b9a0, 0237ba30, 0237bbf0, 0237bcb0, 0237bd00, at 90% HP and at 30%
step_2_the_pointed_to_blocks.result: only the FIRST (0237b9a0, the one at entity+0xD4) changes at all — 16 of 32 words. The other four are byte-identical.
step_2_the_pointed_to_blocks.control: with HP HELD at 90% over three samples, only 1 of 32 words moves on its own (+0x4C). So the 16 were not idle churn over the sampling interval.

*** THE APPARENT THRESHOLD AT 40-45% IS.what_it_looked_like: sweeping 90..30% the block flipped together between 45% and 40%: +0x24/+0x28 0x400->0x800, +0x2C 0x19a->0x14, +0x04 gained the pointer 0237cb90, +0x08 began counting, +0x0C/+0x18 went non-zero. Latch-shaped, and it would have been reported as B2's answer.
*** THE APPARENT THRESHOLD AT 40-45% IS.what_killed_it: a bisect. Stepping HP 760, 742, 730, 720, 710, 700, 690, 680, 670, 660 — ten samples straight through the supposed trigger — produced NO transition: +0x24 stayed 0x400 and +0x2C stayed 0x19a throughout. Raising HP back to 900, 1200, 1485 produced no reversion either, so it is not a latch that had already fired.
*** THE APPARENT THRESHOLD AT 40-45% IS.so: the flip was an EVENT in time that happened to fall between two samples of a descending sweep. The block is event-driven, not HP-driven. The 16-word difference at step 2 is the same artefact accumulated over a longer interval, and the 3-sample control was simply too short to catch it.
*** THE APPARENT THRESHOLD AT 40-45% IS.lesson: a monotone sweep cannot tell 'changed because of X' from 'changed while X was being changed'. Only the bisect, and the failure to revert, separates them.

B2_LIVE_SWEEP_2026_08_01.superseded_2026_10_11: The historical experiment watched0237B9A0 as a controller, but live breakpoint ownership proves the AI controller is0237BEA0 at entity+10. Its broad no-phase conclusion is withdrawn. See live_correction_2026_10_11.

B2_ANSWERED_2026_08_02_REAL_DAMAGE.what: B2 settled. The previous session showed WRITING HP cannot answer it and named the experiment that could: cross the threshold with REAL damage. This is that experiment.
B2_ANSWERED_2026_08_02_REAL_DAMAGE.the_method_that_works: the savestate's fight is live — the party keeps attacking, so HP falls on its own at roughly 5-10 per second. So seed HP to just ABOVE a candidate threshold and let the game's own damage carry it across. The crossing then goes through the damage-apply path, which is exactly what a written HP bypasses. Snapshot entity+0x000..+0x140 and the controller at 0x0237B9A0 either side.

max_over_2 (Octo's rule).entity_head: 0 words changed, excluding HP and position
max_over_2 (Octo's rule).controller_0237b9a0: 1 word changed, +0x4C — the word already known to free-run

35_percent (psz-godot's assumption).entity_head: 0 words changed, excluding HP and position

B2_ANSWERED_2026_08_02_REAL_DAMAGE.*** THE INSTRUMENT CONTROL, which is wha: a negative is worthless if the thing being watched never moves. Over 15 consecutive 0.5s intervals of live play the entity head changed in 8 of them — so it is NOT inert. And the only head words that EVER moved are +0xD0 (5 intervals) and +0xEC (4), both while HP sat still at 399. The controller's +0x4C moved in 15 of 15. So the head is live, its only movers are the two known free-running fields, and neither is a function of HP.
B2_ANSWERED_2026_08_02_REAL_DAMAGE.*** THE ANSWER ***: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-11: the old broad no-phase conclusion used an incorrectly identified controller.
